concepts.def: Permanent removal of forest for other land uses.
Cheap oil grown on plantations replacing rainforests.

walkthroughs.body_html: The biggest drivers of deforestation are cattle ranching, soybean farming, palm oil plantations, mining, urbanisation and infrastructure such as roads. In the Amazon, cattle ranching accounts for over 70 percent of forest loss. In Indonesia and Malaysia, palm oil dominates. Tropical forests lose around 10 million hectares per year globally.

The Amazon rainforest is around 5.5 million km2 across nine countries, with about 60 percent in Brazil. Roughly 17 percent has already been lost. Beef and soy exports are key drivers, with feedback loops where roads enable more clearing. Scientists warn that 20 to 25 percent loss could trigger Amazon dieback into savanna.

Deforestation releases stored carbon (around 10 percent of global emissions), reduces rainfall by cutting evapotranspiration, destroys habitat for around 80 percent of land species, fuels biodiversity loss and increases soil erosion. Indigenous communities lose homes and food sources. Tropical forest loss also reduces regulation of regional climate.
